title: Uniform cohomology bound under affine morphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. There is $n\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every affine morphism $h:Y\to X$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism], every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent], and every $p\ge n$, the additive group $H^p(Y,F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is zero. The bound is independent of $Y,h,F$.

source.place: Tag 01XJ, lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images, proof of (3), finite affine-cover argument; Tag 08DR induction principle

proof.text: Apply quasi-compact-open induction to P(W): there is n_W bounding H^p(h^{-1}W,F) for every affine h:Y->X and quasi-coherent F on Y. If W is affine, h^{-1}W is affine by the definition of affine morphism. Affine-open vanishing supplies n_W=1.

Given bounds a,b,c for A,B,A intersection B, take max(max(a,b),c)+1 for A union B. Write p=q+1. Both degree-p groups on the inverse images of A and B vanish, and the degree-q group on their intersection vanishes. Mayer-Vietoris exactness makes every union class the image of an intersection class, hence zero. Preimage preserves unions and intersections. This proves the induction gluing hypothesis uniformly in h and F. The Lean induction step applies the existing public RingedSpace.module_mayerVietoris directly; it declares no duplicate private union theorem.

Take W=top. Compute open module cohomology at top using one injective module resolution. Its section complex is the forgetful image of the module global-section complex; exact forgetful functor preserves homology. Transport zero cohomology to module right-derived sections and then along the additive source-cohomology comparison to H^p(Y,F).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_affine_pullback_openCohomology_bound (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ {Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : Y ⟶ X) [IsAffineHom h]
      (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent], ∀ p : ℕ, n ≤ p →
        Subsingleton (F.H p)
